content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Azure Networking: Virtual Networks (VNets), Subnets, and NSGs/ASGs"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Welcome to this technical tutorial on foundational Microsoft Azure networking components. Properly designing your Virtual Networks (VNets), segmenting with Subnets, and securing traffic with Network Security Groups (NSGs) and Application Security Groups (ASGs) is critical for building robust, scalable, and secure cloud architectures."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Azure Virtual Networks (VNets)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"An Azure Virtual Network (VNet) is the fundamental building block for your private network in Azure. A VNet enables many types of Azure resources, such as Azure Virtual Machines (VM), to securely communicate with each other, the internet, and on-premises networks."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"az network vnet create --resource-group MyResourceGroup --name MyVNet --address-prefix 10.0.0.0/16"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Subnets: Segmenting Your VNet"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Subnets allow you to segment your VNet into one or more interconnected sub-networks. This enables you to organize your resources, apply specific routing rules, and enforce security policies at a granular level."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Public Subnets: Connected directly to the internet via an Azure Route Table and a Gateway or Load Balancer."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Private Subnets: Isolated from direct inbound internet traffic, typically used for databases and backend application logic."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"az network vnet subnet create --resource-group MyResourceGroup --vnet-name MyVNet --name FrontendSubnet --address-prefix 10.0.1.0/24"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Network Security Groups (NSGs)"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"An NSG contains security rules that allow or deny inbound network traffic to, or outbound network traffic from, several types of Azure resources. You can apply NSGs to subnets, individual VMs, or network interfaces (NICs)."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"az network nsg rule create --resource-group MyResourceGroup --nsg-name MyNsg --name AllowHTTP --priority 100 --direction Inbound --access Allow --protocol Tcp --destination-port-ranges 80"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Application Security Groups (ASGs)"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Application Security Groups enable you to configure network security as a natural extension of an application structure, allowing you to group virtual machines and define network security policies based on those groups. You can reuse your security policy at scale without manually maintaining explicit IP addresses."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Create an ASG for your web tier and another for your database tier."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Apply the ASG directly to the network interface of the respective virtual machines."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Reference the ASG directly in your NSG rules instead of defining individual IP ranges."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"az network asg create --resource-group MyResourceGroup --name WebASG --location eastus"},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining VNets, Subnets, NSGs, and ASGs, you establish a defense-in-depth architecture in Azure. Always ensure your design follows the principle of least privilege, isolating sensitive data tiers into private subnets protected by finely tuned ASG-based NSG rules."}]
